name: Test Coverage Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday test coverage work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical test coverage tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday test coverage work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical test coverage tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious test coverage decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. When multiple test coverage strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. When test coverage decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. When test coverage guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Measure before optimizing any test coverage bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. Keep test coverage changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. State assumptions about test coverage explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop test coverage edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of test coverage correctness.
- Avoid introducing new test coverage abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting test coverage assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated test coverage concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for test coverage, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
